subject: Annual token commitment options and flexibility overview
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Barnes <erin@arcadialabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Annual token commitment options and flexibility overview

Hi Erin —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our ask, I put together three recommended annual commit structures for Arcadia Labs' hosted API usage. The attached one-pager (20270420-jasmine-token-commit-summary.pdf) summarizes the mechanics; key points below so you can skim quickly.

Quick summary (list prices are per-token baseline; discounts applied to hosted API list):
- Starter: 2M tokens/year commit — 15% discount; no carryover; 30-day ramp allowed. Aimed at small pilot teams.
- Growth (recommended): 25M tokens/year commit — 35% discount; up to 20% carryover year-over-year; smoothing credits for quarter-to-quarter ramp. 6-month staged ramp path included.
- Enterprise: 200M+ tokens/year commit — 45%+ tiered discount, committed capacity priority, SLA credits, and optional private deployment terms.

Optional levers you asked about:
- Carryover: up to 20% of unused tokens can carry into the next 12 months for Growth; Enterprise can request higher carryover on a case-by-case basis.
- Smoothing: we can provide monthly credit smoothing to avoid spikes counting against the commit in the first year.
- Breakpoints: discounts scale at 10M, 50M, 200M token thresholds; we can model a blended rate for non-standard volumes.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Tell me which tier most closely matches your budget runway (pilot vs aggressive scale).
2) I will send a short term sheet and proposed DocuSign link for approvals + procurement flow.

Attached: one-pager + term sheet stub. If you want, we can set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the numbers.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: 20270420-jasmine-token-commit-summary.pdf (presentation), redwood-term-sheet-arcadia.docx (term sheet stub)

From: Erin Barnes <erin@arcadialabs.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@arcadialabs.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Annual token commitment options and flexibility overview

Thanks Jasmine — this is very helpful. A few quick clarifying Qs before we loop finance/procurement: 

1) Ramp profile: the Growth example looks sensible, but our usage will likely be front-loaded in Q2 and Q3. Can the 6-month staged ramp be front-weighted without losing the smoothing credits?
2) Carryover mechanics: does the 20% carryover apply only to the Growth tier or could we negotiate a pilot-year exception if we sign an Enterprise commitment in year 2?
3) Refunds/credits: if we materially underuse the commit after 9 months (e.g., <50% of forecast), what remedial credit options do you offer?

Procurement — please confirm what paperwork you need from our side (PO templates, vendor form, certificate of insurance, W-9). We will likely need a standard SLA appendix and data processing addendum for security.

Appreciate the speedy turnaround.

—Erin
VP Product, Arcadia Labs

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Annual token commitment options and flexibility overview

Erin —

Great questions. Short answers first, then a proposed recommended structure for Arcadia: 

1) Ramp profile: yes, we can front-weight the 6-month ramp and still apply smoothing credits. The smoothing is effectively a monthly credit pool for the first 12 months; we will model your expected Q2/Q3 skew and produce a monthly burn schedule so you don't hit overage early.

2) Carryover: Growth tier includes a standard 20% carryover. For year-1 exceptions where you sign Growth in year 1 and move to Enterprise in year 2, we can offer a one-time additional carryover concession (up to another 10%) as part of a conversion incentive.

3) Remedial credits: If usage is <50% of forecast after 9 months, we offer either (a) smoothing credits to apply to the next quarter, or (b) a partial credit to the following year's invoice up to 10% of the committed value. This is meant to protect you from aggressive forecasting risk.

Our recommended plan for Arcadia (we believe this balances runway, cost, and flexibility):
- Start: Growth tier at 25M tokens/year commit; blended effective discount ~38% in year 1 (we can model exact blended rate once we have monthly burn).
- Ramp: front-weighted 6-month ramp (40% of year commit in first two quarters combined), with monthly smoothing credits to avoid early overage.
- Convert path: explicit conversion clause to Enterprise terms if you exceed 80% of annual commit for two consecutive quarters; includes a one-time carryover top-up as noted.
- Procurement/Docs: I'll attach a short term sheet and DocuSign envelope after you confirm.

Attached are the updated term sheet and a draft DocuSign envelope. If this looks good, I'll run pricing approval with Marissa for a final one-off concession (Erin mentioned competitive alternative vs their incumbent).

Best —
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-term-sheet-arcadia.docx (updated), DocuSign link (placeholder)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Annual token commitment options and flexibility overview

Jasmine / Karthik —

Thanks for the draft and the flexibility language. For a new logo with Arcadia's profile, I can approve an override to shaded list pricing but need Vivek to OK a conditional one-time concession. Proposed internal authorization: up to 30% effective discount in year 1 for Growth (instead of the 35% list we quoted), with the following guardrails:
- 12-month minimum term; commit is non-cancellable.
- Carryover capped at 20% for year 1; additional carryover on conversion only with explicit finance sign-off.
- No retroactive refunds; remedial credits as Jasmine outlined are available via invoice credit.

Vivek — can you confirm whether we should include SLA credit language at 0.5% daily uptime breach with a 30-day cure window, or push for 1% per day to align Enterprise more strictly? Also confirm DocuSign envelope routing (legal -> finance -> procurement).

If Vivek signs off, Jasmine please send the DocuSign packet to Erin and cc procurement.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

-- internal note: hold pricing approval until Vivek confirms SLA exposure.
